payload.because: The home is ALREADY in the truth log — session_started names it uniquely — so an index file would be duplicated state that can desync, needs pruning (99 sessions and counting), and forces a SPEC Record-layout change plus a gitignore decision (routing is a local runtime fact, but .sofar/ is committed wholesale). Deriving costs one file read on the common path (branch is correct → hit on the first log checked) and only pays the sibling scan in exactly the case where a misroute would otherwise have happened; total log volume is ~350KB. It is also self-healing: sessions registered before this fix get pinned correctly with no migration. Same philosophy as reading git state rather than logging it — a fact with an authoritative home is read, never copied.
payload.chose: Derive a session's home initiative from the event logs themselves — scan for the session's earliest session_started, checking the branch-bound initiative first and only falling through to siblings on a miss
payload.over: A new .sofar/sessions.json index mapping session_id to slug, written at registration and read by hooks

payload.because: Measuring the 14 double-registrations in this repo inverted the hypothesis: 11 are hook-then-claude-code across two initiatives, i.e. the tear is NOT mostly a mid-session branch switch but lazy registration racing start_session — the hook registers in the branch's initiative, the binding moves, and start_session registers the SAME id again elsewhere. Hook pinning alone would have left those 11 intact. The source-based heuristic was rejected by the same data: the second registration is usually claude-code, so treating claude-code as deliberate would suppress 11 of 14 real splits.
payload.chose: Pin start_session to the session home as well as the hooks — branch resolution now applies only when `initiative` is explicit or the session has no home
payload.over: Pinning hooks alone (the original Phase 1 scope), or using envelope.source to tell a deliberate re-home from a misroute

payload.because: User ruling: the pin handles everything going forward, so retro-repair buys nothing. But a permanently red doctor trains people to ignore it, and 0/3450 events carry any self-evident misplacement marker (envelope.initiative always matches its directory), so repair would be inferential anyway — asserting a guess as a correction event is worse than leaving accurate history. Liveness is the honest severity axis: an ended split is settled and unfixable by construction, while an open one is a pre-fix session still actively tearing and worth blocking on.
payload.chose: Accept the 21 pre-existing splits as history — no correction-event repair — and grade doctor's session-routing findings by LIVENESS: FAIL only when a split involves a session still open, WARN when every session in it has ended
payload.over: Repairing the splits with correction events, or leaving every split at FAIL

payload.because: Reattribution is not expressible in this log's semantics. correction events VOID by ref (fold.ts pass 1) — they delete, they cannot move — and replay order is normatively ulid order (task 13.1, D-sync-1) so replicas converge. A re-appended event therefore carries a fresh ulid encoding now and sorts to the END of the target log, folding after that session's session_ended and after every task that was active at the real time. That fabricates a timeline that never happened, which is strictly worse than accurate history filed in the wrong place. Closing 40742c6d is different in kind: the session genuinely ended without a write-back in July, so session_closed asserts only what is true, and it takes doctor from 1 FAIL to exit 0.
payload.chose: Repair scope = close the one abandoned session (40742c6d in harness-build) and nothing else; reattributing the 780 leaked events is rejected as unsound
payload.over: Voiding leaked events in their wrong initiative and re-appending them into the right one
